operations.before: [F2] The reverse-kernel generator and compact-test martingale identity are obtained from the forward density equation and justified differentiation under its transition integrals. [[lem-reversed-kernels-and-generator-identity]]
operations.after: [F2] If an auxiliary reverse Itô solution has spacetime absolutely continuous stopped occupation measures and initial density $p_T$, the classical forward density equations identify its law and kernels with the actual reversed process. The proof uses positive mixtures of $q/p$, conservation, time averaging, and a fixed-endpoint $L^1$ limit. [[lem-forward-density-duality-identifies-reverse-process]]

[F7] A continuous semimartingale with uniformly positive bracket density has spacetime absolutely continuous occupation measure after stopping to make expected drift variation and bracket trace finite; no bounded initial value or squared-drift condition is required. [[lem-stopped-uniformly-elliptic-semimartingale-occupation-absolute-continuity]]

It gives, for every compactly supported smooth $\phi$, the reverse generator $\displaystyle \widetilde L_u\phi(y)=p_{T-u}(y)^{-1}\{L_{T-u}^*(p_{T-u}\phi)(y)-\phi(y)L_{T-u}^*p_{T-u}(y)\}$ and the corresponding compensated local martingale. operations.after: 2.1 Choose an auxiliary nonexplosive continuous solution $Z$ of the assumed reverse martingale problem, with initial density $p_T$. Compact coordinate cutoffs give $Z=Z_0+\int\widetilde b\,du+N$ locally in state, with $N$ a continuous local martingale. Coordinate-product cutoffs and [F4] identify $[N]_u=\int_0^u a_{T-v}(Z_v)dv$: subtract the two product compensators and use that a continuous finite-variation local martingale is constant. The compact-test integrals make the local drift and trace integrals finite; nonexplosion and continuity exhaust the finite interval, without a bound on $Z_0$. Work in the usual augmentation, which preserves these continuous local martingales by the stopped event-test argument in the proof of [F5]. Left-step approximations as in [F6] give a predictable version of $\sigma_{T-u}(Z_u)$, and [F5] constructs the auxiliary Brownian Itô representation with the same drift and bracket. If $C=\sup\|\sigma^{-1}\|$, then $a\ge C^{-2}I$. Stop when $|Z|$ or the accumulated drift-plus-trace energy reaches $n$; the stops exhaust $T$ and the expected stopped variation and trace are finite. Thus [F7] supplies their occupation absolute continuity. Apply [F2], using only the original classical forward equations for $q,p$ and the actual forward path continuity: it identifies all marginals and Bayes kernels of $Z$ with those of $Y$, and transfers the compact-test local martingale problem to $Y$ in its natural reversed filtration. In particular the displayed operator is its extended martingale generator. [F2, F4, F5, F6, F7, step 1.1]

[F3] For symmetric $a$, the formal adjoint product rule is
$$p^{-1}\{L_t^*(p\phi)-\phi L_t^*p\}=\left(-b_i+p^{-1}\partial_j(pa_{ij})\right)\partial_i\phi+\tfrac12a_{ij}\partial_{ij}\phi.$$
Thus the first-order coefficient is $-b+\nabla\!\cdot a+a\nabla\log p$. [[lem-reversed-kernels-and-generator-identity]]
